messages:
Anika: Quick thread — proposing a zonal soft-start for variant v3 (per-tenant opt-in). Goal: let caches warm + observe tail latency before broad traffic. Sketch below, need ops + SRE signoff.
TJ: Can you outline the rollout slices and the rollback triggers? also, do we need any per-tenant opt-out windows? :thinking_face:
Anika: Short plan:
- Phase 0: shadow traffic (all regions) for 24h
- Phase 1: 1% of tenants in west-us (zonal) for 4h
- Phase 2: 5% of tenants in west-us + 1% east-us for 8h
- Phase 3: 20% spread across EU/US for 24h
- Phase 4: gradual full ramp with canary monitors
Per-tenant opt-in via a feature flag gate.
Rafael: Sounds reasonable. For the per-tenant opt-in we should require explicit consent + a minimum token budget. We should also mark tenants as "warmable" so cache priming jobs run ahead of traffic.
SRE-Amber: Rollback/kill conditions I care about:
- p99 generation latency > 150ms sustained for 5m
- error rate >= 0.5% (5xx / total requests) over 5m
- model degradation signals (BLEU/drop in eval metric) flagged by /quality-alerts
- unexpected token cost delta > +20% vs baseline
If any of these hit, auto-fail to variant fallback and notify oncall.
TJ: Agree. Also add circuit-breaker on queue length and memory pressure per-node. If queue length > 200 or GPU mem pressure > 85% for 3m, drop traffic.
Anika: Example feature-flag payload we expect ops to support (for per-tenant gating):
```json
{
  "flag": "model_variant_v3",
  "tenants": ["tenant-123", "tenant-456"],
  "region": "west-us",
  "pct": 1,
  "start": "2026-04-02T14:00:00Z",
  "end": null
}
```
Rafael: ops-bot should be able to toggle that flag and run the priming job. Suggested priming job: `scripts/prime_cache.sh --tenant tenant-123 --model v3 --tokens 2000` and mark history in the rollout ledger.
ops-bot: deploy: feature-flag-service v2.3 rolled to staging at 2026-03-30T09:12Z :white_check_mark:
SRE-Amber: Also: add a heatmap dashboard for per-tenant p95/p99, token-cost-per-tenant, and model-fallback-count. We want automatic ticketing to #incidents if rollback triggers fire.
TJ: For A/B measurement: run an experiment comparing v2 baseline vs v3 on a small holdout group. Track latency, cost, and top-5 hallucination signals. Use the `ab-runner` job with these knobs:
```
ab-runner --control v2 --variant v3 --metric-lag 24h --min-sample 2000
```
Anika: How about canary timing windows? I'm thinking rolling windows overlapping by 50% to avoid cold-start cliffs. E.g., schedule 4h windows but start new slices every 2h.
Rafael: Good idea. Also, implement fallback chaining: primary->compatible-quantized->v2. If primary fails, try quantized; if quantized fails, fallback to v2 with sticky fallback for 5m to avoid oscillation.
SRE-Amber: Can we codify failover with these constraints: sticky-fallback=300s, rapid-escalation if >3 rollbacks in 30m for same tenant -> block tenant from variant for 24h.
Anika: Noted. Owner map for playbook draft: product=Anika, eng-platform=TJ, ops=Rafael, oncall=SRE-Amber. Next steps: TJ to add circuit-breaker hooks, Rafael to add priming + flag API, Amber to create dashboards and PagerDuty runbook. I'll schedule a 30m shiproom for signoff.
TJ: I'll put PRs up for the hooks today and link here. :thumbsup:
Rafael: I'll sketch the priming job and flag API contract. ETA EOD tomorrow.
SRE-Amber: I'll stub alerts and runbook, link to runbook template in #incidents.
Anika: Thanks team — final ask: please add any constraints (legal/enterprise) if tenant opt-in requires KMS or data residency checks. If none, I'll move to calendar invite.
TJ: One more: for Dedicated customers, we should surface an override so they can opt-out at org level. Add `org_override: true` to the flag schema.
Anika: Good call. I'll include that in the playbook draft. Meeting invite incoming. :calendar:
